Projection for 2027: try your own assumptions

Irish quotas and values for 2027 worked out the same way as Part 2 of the Quota Calculator (v1.2). It starts from the workbook's own settings; change any assumption and the totals update. Nothing you change here is saved.

StockTAC 2026Ireland 2026Advice 2027AssumptionTAC 2027Ireland 2027ChangeHagueValue 2027

Tonnes. "Use my assumptions" applies the rollover or percentage set for a stock; with it off, every stock follows the ICES advice as in the workbook, and stocks with no advice are left out. Values use the workbook's prices, with mackerel at the price above; the 2026 value counts only stocks that have a 2027 figure, so the two years compare like for like. Landing obligation adjustments are as set in the workbook.

ICES areas and divisions

The statistical areas ICES uses for advice and the EU uses for TACs. A TAC code such as COD/07A. refers to division 7a, the Irish Sea. Shading shows landings of the stock selected in the landings panel below, or the Irish share of them. Tap a division to see what is landed there and to filter the landings panel to that division.

Irish seafood sector in 2024 (BIM)

Headline figures from BIM, The Business of Seafood 2024. Landings data from the SFPA, valued by BIM; quota from the Official Journal. Some figures are provisional and rounded.

Landings into Irish ports by port, 2024

PortValueTonnes€ per tonne

What BIM says

  • Landings into Irish ports rose 11% to nearly 300,000 tonnes, but a third came from foreign vessels, mainly pelagic landings into Killybegs. The value of Irish landings rose 4%.
  • Nephrops and mackerel alone account for nearly half the value of Irish landings; mackerel prices reached record highs, but quota cuts limited the benefit to the fleet.
  • The demersal sector saw a 14% fall in value, with whitefish held back by early-season weather and limited quota.
  • Quota for 2025: 182,000 tonnes worth an estimated €247m, up 3% in volume but down 2% in value. Cuts to mackerel (-16%) and blue whiting (-14%) were offset by horse mackerel (+416%); Area 6 demersal quotas rose 29%.
